title: Reserve Funding Crisis in U.S. Nonprofits
description: Financial stability matters. 48% of nonprofits lack adequate emergency reserves.

slides.headline: The Reserve Crisis
slides.subheadline: What 1.7M nonprofits tell us about financial stability.

slides.label: Part 1: The Problem
slides.headline: Nearly Half Can't Survive a Funding Gap
slides.story: When a major grant ends or a funder withdraws, nonprofits with weak reserves cannot survive the gap. Nearly half the sector faces this vulnerability. Programs shut down. Staff are laid off. Community suffers.

slides.label: Part 2: Who's Vulnerable
slides.headline: Small Orgs Have Zero Cushion
slides.accent_label: Nonprofits with Less Than 3 Months of Operating Funds
slides.story: Organizations under $500K invest every dollar directly into programs—which is admirable. But it leaves zero cushion. One funding disruption shuts down critical services. Small nonprofits are one crisis away from collapse.

slides.label: Part 3: The Solution
slides.headline: Strategic Reserve Funding Multiplies Impact
slides.story: Funders who support reserve-building don't just save organizations—they multiply impact. A nonprofit with 6 months of reserves can weather storms, plan long-term, and serve communities with confidence. Strategic reserve grants are force multipliers.

slides.headline: Fund Reserves. Stabilize Impact.
body_lines: See which nonprofits need reserves most.
